angle: Falling spend can be healthy—if it reflects learning curves and sharper ROI, not apathy.
sourceTitle: AI spend per employee slumped at top firms in August — summer doldrums or a warning sign?
linkedinPost:
AI spend per employee is slipping. Panic… or progress?

TechCrunch reports that August saw a dip as token prices fell, cheaper models spread, and usage cooled. From the trenches, lower spend can be a good sign—if it reflects the learning curve from “explore everywhere” to “scale what works.”

In mature rollouts I’ve led, unit costs fall while value rises because teams:
- Consolidate to a few proven use cases with P&L owners.
- Right-size models and context windows to the job-to-be-done.
- Cache, batch, and precompute to cut waste without hurting CX.

Red flags are different: abandoned dashboards, orphaned pilots, and no business metrics tied to usage.

My take: Don’t track AI success by gross spend. Track cost-to-serve, handle time, conversion, deflection, and NPS next to model costs. If spend drops and outcomes hold or improve, that’s maturity—not malaise.

How are you separating disciplined efficiency from fading interest in your AI program?
xPost: Falling AI spend/employee isn’t doom if outcomes hold. Mature teams right-size models, cache/batch, and scale only what moves P&L. Measure CX + costs next to tokens, not vanity usage. #AIStrategy #EnterpriseAI
